items.scene: A box is labeled "cookies." Mia watches Raj take the cookies out and put crayons inside. Later, Eli only sees the closed box.
items.question: What will Eli think is inside the box?
items.why_this_case_matters: Direct appearance-reality match: Eli has only the label and surface appearance, not the hidden switch.

items.scene: A jar has a jam label on it. Priya sees her brother switch the jam for peanut butter and close it again.
items.question: What is really inside the jar now?
items.why_this_case_matters: Tests objective reality despite misleading packaging and a witnessed substitution.

items.scene: Sam leaves the room. While Sam is gone, Zoe moves the toy bear from the basket to the drawer. Sam comes back and asks where the bear is.
items.question: Where will Sam look first?
items.why_this_case_matters: This is a false-belief search-location task, a near miss that should route to macro-01 instead.

items.scene: During a talk, a student says, "Fine, go ahead" and gives a quick wink.
items.question: What is the wink mainly meant to signal?
items.why_this_case_matters: The key evidence is a nonverbal cue, so this is a boundary case for macro-04 rather than appearance-reality.
